requirement_paraphrase: Clinical benefits and risks should be used to set clinically meaningful performance goals for testing, with attention to global and local performance and input and output variability.

framework: Good Machine Learning Practice for Medical Device Development: Guiding Principles (Health Canada page, published 27 October 2021, last modified 29 July 2024)
clause_or_page: Principle 08, testing under clinically relevant conditions
requirement_paraphrase: Test plans should be statistically sound and generate clinically relevant performance data independent of the training set, covering the intended population, important subgroups and confounding factors.

framework: DoD Directive 3000.09, Autonomy in Weapon Systems (reissued 25 January 2023)

framework: DoD Directive 3000.09, Autonomy in Weapon Systems (reissued 25 January 2023)
requirement_paraphrase: Before formal development, an autonomous weapon system outside the exempt categories needs senior approval (USD(P), USD(R&E), VCJCS); the officials verify plans exist for V&V and T&E to establish reliability, effectiveness and suitability under realistic conditions, including possible adversary actions.

framework: DoD Directive 3000.09, Autonomy in Weapon Systems (reissued 25 January 2023)
requirement_paraphrase: Before fielding, senior reviewers verify that system performance, capability, reliability, effectiveness and suitability have been assessed under realistic conditions; Sec. 4.1.d(3)(b) also asks for a demonstration that the system can be reprogrammed quickly enough.

framework: SR 11-7, Supervisory Guidance on Model Risk Management (dated 4 April 2011, last updated 19 August 2011 per page)
requirement_paraphrase: Validation covers evaluation of conceptual soundness (design, construction, documentation, empirical support), ongoing monitoring to confirm the model performs as intended, and outcomes analysis comparing model outputs with actual outcomes, including back-testing.

framework: SR 11-7, Supervisory Guidance on Model Risk Management (dated 4 April 2011, last updated 19 August 2011 per page)
clause_or_page: Section 'Model Validation', independence passage (locator not seen)
requirement_paraphrase: Validation should involve a degree of independence from model development and use, generally performed by staff not responsible for development or use.

framework: SR 26-2, Revised Guidance on Model Risk Management (issued 17 April 2026)
clause_or_page: Section V (Model Validation and Monitoring), p. 9
requirement_paraphrase: Validation generally occurs before a model's first use; if urgent business need forces earlier use, the institution should attend to limitations and apply controls such as usage limits or closer monitoring.

framework: SR 26-2, Revised Guidance on Model Risk Management (issued 17 April 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Model testing is a core part of development; it can include out-of-sample and out-of-time testing, comparison of alternative assumptions and assessment of data quality, with rigour matched to complexity and materiality.

framework: CFPB Consumer Financial Protection Circular 2022-03 (published 26 May 2022)
requirement_paraphrase: Creditors may use post-hoc explanation methods but, because these approximate models, must still be able to validate the accuracy of the approximations, which may not be possible with less interpretable models.

requirement_paraphrase: Begin testing on infrastructure built for testing, start with low fidelity tests for fast iteration, move to more realistic non-production systems including hardware in the loop, and move into production for further testing only after sufficient non-production testing; keep production data out of test environments.

framework: Principles for the Secure Integration of Artificial Intelligence in Operational Technology (CISA, ASD ACSC and partners, initial version 3 December 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: Regularly assess AI functions and test their resilience through offensive security exercises (red teaming), and continuously validate and refine AI models in simulated environments before deployment.

framework: Principles for the Secure Integration of Artificial Intelligence in Operational Technology (CISA, ASD ACSC and partners, initial version 3 December 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: Treat AI systems like any new OT system and test them for safety impacts such as latency and interoperability, using test infrastructure before production deployment where possible, and provide failsafe reversion to traditional automation or manual control.

framework: Texas H.B. 149, Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act (Senate Committee Report version, committee substitute)

framework: Texas H.B. 149, Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act (Senate Committee Report version, committee substitute)
requirement_paraphrase: The department must create a regulatory sandbox where an approved person can test an AI system for a limited time and on a limited basis without a licence or other authorisation, for up to 36 months.

requirement_paraphrase: The principle gives, as examples of transparency, comprehensive testing of planned changes and monitoring of, and response to, performance deviations.

framework: US NIST AI 200-2 ipd (The TEVV-Athlon Framework, initial public draft, August 2026)

framework: US NIST SP 800-218A (SSDF Community Profile for generative AI, July 2024)

framework: US NIST SP 800-218A (SSDF Community Profile for generative AI, July 2024)

framework: US NIST SP 800-218A (SSDF Community Profile for generative AI, July 2024)
requirement_paraphrase: Recommends frequent scanning and testing of AI models for undetected vulnerabilities after release and periodic audits.

framework: US OMB M-25-22 (Driving Efficient Acquisition of AI in Government, 3 April 2025)
clause_or_page: Sec. 4(e) Contract Administration, item i Authorization To Operate Compliance (p. 11)
requirement_paraphrase: AI systems and services operated as an information system by or on behalf of an agency must receive an authorization to operate from an appropriate agency official before deployment.

framework: US OMB M-25-22 (Driving Efficient Acquisition of AI in Government, 3 April 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: Where practicable, agencies should seek detailed demonstrations and tests of AI products in realistic environments before award.

framework: US OMB M-25-22 (Driving Efficient Acquisition of AI in Government, 3 April 2025)
clause_or_page: Sec. 4(d) Contract Terms, item F Vendor Performance Requirements (p. 10)
requirement_paraphrase: Agencies are encouraged to require vendors to meet performance standards before deployment, and to monitor performance with rollback options.

framework: US White House America's AI Action Plan (July 2025)
clause_or_page: Pillar I, Build an AI Evaluations Ecosystem (p. 10)
requirement_paraphrase: Directs NIST/CAISI to publish guidelines so agencies can conduct their own AI evaluations, support evaluation science, and convene evaluation-practice meetings; policy goals for government, not obligations on developers.

framework: US White House America's AI Action Plan (July 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: Calls for AI testbeds for piloting AI systems in secure real-world settings and for CAISI-led national security evaluations of frontier models with developers.
